subject: Addendum to 230b80f3: Ziggy's ruling on naming the author in the story (the meta way); RESEARCH_VALIS section 5 revised and rehashed
body:
Ziggy, in the session after a gap (recorded at 10:04 UTC by the clock), asked whether the story could reference Philip K. Dick and his novel directly, in a meta way, giving credit rather than taking it. The writer's assessment, given to him in chat: yes; naming a real author and a real book as homage and fact is ordinary and clean; what credit never buys is the work itself (his people, plot, scenes, long prose); for the films as art pieces this is standard practice, and a wide commercial release needs a lawyer's clearance read, which the writer cannot give. He ruled on the proposed rule with one word: "Word."

The rule, now RESEARCH_VALIS_20261013.md section 5 (replacing the first draft's "never in a script or prompt"): (1) the author and his novel may be named in dialogue and on-screen text as a real author and a real book; the fiction's network may be called VALIS and say in-story that it was named after the book, as the real research project did; (2) quotation stays to a line, attributed inside the dialogue or on-screen text itself (the four-word line the fleet greeting opens on qualifies; the acronym's expansion, if spoken, is spoken as his); (3) none of the novel's people, plot or scenes; (4) no implied blessing from the author's estate; (5) the research handle stays Ziggy's; the charter, invocation and couplet are his text; (6) the scale caution recorded with the ruling. Open item 14's fourth question (the fleet's name in the fiction) is resolved by it.

Still nothing generated, published, spent or activated; masters, reviews, roles and timing untouched. CFA Nova reads this at her checkpoint.
